title: A Dose History the Endocrinologist Can Actually Read | vitalii.no
description:
Every insulin dose Artem's parents calculated used to live only in their heads or on a scrap of paper. There was no record to show the doctor at the next appointment, no history of how the doctor's own correction settings had changed over time, and estimating carbs for an unfamiliar meal meant guessing from a nutrition label in a language nobody at the table could read quickly.

A full calculator now sits behind Google sign-in. Every calculated dose is written to a journal so parents can scroll back through past days, the doctor's settings — correction factor, target range — are versioned with timestamps instead of overwritten, and a photo of a meal or its label can be sent to an AI vision call that returns an estimated carbohydrate count straight into the dose field.

Artem's parents now have a timestamped dose and settings history they can hand the endocrinologist instead of reconstructing it from memory, and carb entry for a new meal takes one photo instead of a label lookup.
